proof_summary: After division by \((n-1)!\), each fixed inclusion–exclusion summand tends to \((-2)^k/k!\); a summable exponential bound permits passage through the sum, yielding the positive limit \(e^{-2}\) (and hence the same limit after taking the absolute value). The correction series tends to zero by a second dominated-convergence argument, while \(n/(n-2)\to1\), so the proposed expression has the same normalized nonzero limit and their ratio tends to one.
